title: LIVE ICE TYPE
noaa_source: U.S. National Ice Center (NAIS) daily Great Lakes ice analysis, SIGRID-3 shapefile
product_name: U.S. National Ice Center (NAIS) daily Great Lakes ice analysis, SIGRID-3 shapefile
variable: predominant WMO stage of development (SA/SB/SC by partial concentration)
data_time_utc: NIC analysis date 2026-05-16 (from NIC filename; retrieved 2026-09-22 12:34 UTC)
spatial_resolution_source: NIC SIGRID-3 vector analysis (variable polygon size)
spatial_resolution_rendered: 1800x1175 canvas over lon [-93.0,-73.5], lat [40.5,49.5] (mean-value binning, no upsampling of source precision)
missing_data_treatment: open water (CT<1) fully transparent; unknown/unstaged ice gets the explicit Unknown color, never a real type color.
shoreline_mask: assets/great_lakes_watermask.png — shared NOAA medium-resolution shoreline water mask (nautical-chart compilation, mean-high-water datum; snapped + polygonized once, full vertex precision, antialiased). Overlay alpha is multiplied by this mask and edge RGB is bled into transparent pixels (anti-fringe for bilinear clients), so every product shares one shoreline.

legend_scale_html:
Ice type = predominant WMO stage of development per analysis polygon:
    70 — Brash Ice (thickness not coded in SIGRID-3)
    80 — No Stage of Development (unstaged)
    81 — New Ice (<10 cm)
    82 — Nilas, Ice Rind (<10 cm)
    83 — Young Ice (10-<30 cm)
    84 — Grey Ice (10-<15 cm)
    85 — Grey-White Ice (15-<30 cm)
    86 — First-Year Ice (>=30-200 cm)
    87 — Thin First-Year Ice (30-<70 cm)
    88 — Thin First-Year Ice Stage 1 (30-<50 cm)
    89 — Thin First-Year Ice Stage 2 (50-<70 cm)
    91 — Medium First-Year Ice (70-<120 cm)
    93 — Thick First-Year Ice (>=120 cm (open-ended; 150 cm assumed))
    95 — Old Ice (WMO gives no thickness; no estimate made)
    96 — Second-Year Ice (WMO gives no thickness; no estimate made)
    97 — Multi-Year Ice (WMO gives no thickness; no estimate made)
    98 — Glacier Ice (not applicable (icebergs))
    unknown — Unknown / Undetermined (codes 99, -9)
Open water is transparent; fainter = partial concentration.
data_nature: analyzed (human ice analysis of satellite imagery)
methodology: Per SIGRID-3 polygon: predominant stage = highest partial concentration among SA/SB/SC (ties resolve to the thickest-listed stage); rendered in that stage's fixed key color with pixel alpha scaled by total concentration CT/10. The key lists every WMO stage the dataset supports.
